question.leadin: This man's political supporters were derogatorily nicknamed the descamisados, or "shirtless ones."
question.text: Name this populist president of a South American country who regained power in 1973 after being overthrown in 1955. This man legalized women's suffrage while being influenced by his wife, Evita.
question.clue: This politician's left-wing supporters were killed at an airport in the Ezeiza (ayz-ay-EE-zah) massacre.

swap.text: The US also occupied this country after the Spanish-American War, though they did not annex it. The CIA tried to use an exploding cigar and a tuberculosis-infected scuba suit to kill Fidel Castro, a Communist who led this country during the Cold War.
swap.clue: John F. Kennedy said he wanted to "splinter the CIA into a thousand pieces" after a failed invasion of this country at the Bay of Pigs.

question.leadin: Give the following about the history of Mexico.
question.text: This one-legged dictator of Mexico attempted to crush the Texan Revolution and had that same territory wrested from him in the Mexican-American War.
question.clue: This man launched a coup against his own vice president and held a state funeral for his amputated leg, which was severed during his service in the Pastry War.

swap.leadin: During a coup, this leader committed suicide by AK-47 at the Palacio de La Moneda.
swap.text: Name this socialist leader, who was replaced by the far-right dictator Augusto Pinochet as a result of that coup.
swap.clue: He was a member of the Popular Unity coalition, and defeated Jorge Allesandri to win his highest office.

question.text: With the help of the US, this brutal right-wing dictator assumed power following the death of Salvador Allende.
question.clue: On his 60th birthday, the CIA launched Operation Condor to suppress left-wing movements in this man's nation and neighboring Argentina.

swap.text: A free trade agreement has been put in place by MERCOSUR, for the countries on this continent. This continent is home to protectionist leaders like Cristina Fernandez, Dilma Rousseff, and Nicolas Maduro.
swap.clue: This continent was home to a man who conquered the tribe of Chancas and reorganized his empire into the Tawantinsuyu.

question.leadin: The control of this country's First Republic by two wealthy states led to it being nicknamed for their main products, "coffee and milk."
question.text: Name this country, where that republic was founded by disciples of the positivist sociologist Auguste Comte. This country was later ruled by the populist dictator Getulio Vargas.
question.answerHtml: Brazil [or Federative Republic of Brazil; accept First Brazilian Republic; accept Republic of the United States of Brazil; prompt on Old Republic]
question.clue: After "I Stay Day,"thiscountry's independence was declared with the slogan "Independence or Death," which became known as the Cry ofIpiranga.

swap.leadin: As Secretary of State to Benjamin Harrison, James Blaine attempted to establish a naval base in this country.
swap.text: During that crisis, Rear-Admiral Bancroft Gherardi tried to force this country to cede the town of Mole Saint-Nicolas, but was successfully opposed by this country's President Florvil Hyppolite and its Minister of Foreign Affairs Antenor Firmin.
swap.clue: A non-monarchial ruler of this country had formerly worked as a coachman, and owned several large plantations.

question.text: A charismatic populist, he led the Patriotic Pole alliance after serving two years in prison for a bloody coup against President Carlos Andres Perez in 1992. He has revised the constitution to allow indefinite re-election and sent the police against protestors. For 15 points-name this confidant of Fidel Castro and president of Venezuela.
question.clue: This leader of the Fifth Republic Movement founded the PSUV after a political merger in 2007.

swap.text: Nearly every country in the world signed the Paris Climate accords in 2015, except for two-Syria and this country, led by Daniel Ortega from 1979 to 1990 and again from 2007 to the present.
swap.clue: In 1856, William Walker appointed himself president of this country.

question.leadin: Answer some things related to the rocky beginnings of the Cuban Revolution.
question.text: This Cuban revolutionary led an unsuccessful assault on the Moncada Barracks in 1953. He later had more success in a protracted guerrilla war and became Cuba's communist dictator.
question.clue: This leader noted that "history will absolve me" after attacking the Moncada Barracks, which inspired the name of his "26th of July Movement."

swap.text: This general of Bolivar's served as Bolivia's second president and was victorious at the Battle of Ayacucho. He was killed in 1830, possibly by enemies of Bolivar.
swap.answer: Antonio Jose de Sucre y Alcala
swap.clue: This general led the rebel forces at the Battle of Pichincha. He later helped liberate Peru at the Battle of Ayacucho.

question.text: The Independentist army was led by this man, Simon Bolivar's lieutenant. He would later lend his name to a capital city of Bolivia.
question.clue: After being defeated at the second battle of Huachi, he won a victory over the army of Melchor Aymerich which allowed him to put down resistance in the Pasto province.

swap.leadin: Benjamin Keen examined the "Legacy" of this man, who is the subject of a canonization campaign by Helen Rand Parish.
swap.text: Name this Dominican friar who was appointed Protector of the Indians. He argued against the enslavement of Native Americans in the Valladolid debate.
swap.clue: He's more renowned for appearing at the Council of Valladolid where he engaged in a famous debate after encouraging the passage of the New Laws; his opponent in that debate was Juan Gines de Sepulveda.

question.leadin: While he was a member of a guerrilla organisation, this politician adopted the name Aureliano in homage to a Colonel in One Hundred Years of Solitude.
question.text: Elected in 2022, this politician is the first leftwing President in his country's history, and his vice-president Francia Marquez is the first black woman to hold the post.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about early Spanish colonialism in the Americas.
swap.text: This forced-labor system gave colonists control over a set number of natives, who they nominally agreed to Christianize and clothe in return for de facto slave labor. It was replaced by the repartimiento system.
swap.clue: The repartimiento system was intended as a replacement for this policy, which gave owners a number of natives who worked the land in exchange for being converted to Christianity.

question.leadin: Solon Menos, the Haitian Foreign Minister, fought a duel with the relative of this man following his namesake affair.
question.text: Name this man who's sentencing to one year in prison in Haiti led to two German gunboats arriving at Port-au-Prince demanding compensation, a letter of apology, and a promise that he could return to Haiti.

swap.text: The Paraguayan forces were led by this general, who later served as Paraguayan president before being killed in a 1940 air crash. He drove Paraguayan forces into Bolivian territory, where the war stalled.

question.text: In 1825, this Argentine backed group led by Juan Lavalleja had steadily gained the support of ruler Uruguayans to throw out the Portuguese and dismantle the Cisplatine Republic.
question.answerHtml: Thirty Three Immortals [or Band of 33; or Los treinta y tres; accept equivalents]

swap.text: This island was hit hard by the Great Hurricane of 1780, with one account claiming that it felled and stripped every tree of its bark. Many small landholders forced off their land by large sugar plantations moved from this British island to the Carolinas in the 1670s.
swap.clue: The Bayley plantation was home to a 1816 rebellion of slaves here known as the Bussa Rebellion, and it was the first American location that Oloudah Equiano described.
